newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil parties agree on disputed oil bill clause.
newsitem.headline: Brazil parties agree on disputed oil bill clause.

text.p: A bill opening up Brazil's petroleum industry to private capital was on course for a vote in the Chamber of Deputies later Wednesday after a compromise was reached on a key point, a lawmaker said.

Deputy Jose Carlos Aleluia, a whip with the Liberal Front Party (PFL), said a clause of the bill governing the distribution of fuel and natural gas had been rewritten to avoid a clash between government allies during voting.

A previous version of the bill gave licensed distributors exclusive rights to distribute fuel and natural gas, although thermoelectric power plants, steelmakers, petrochemical and chemical firms were allowed to buy direct from refineries.

Aleluia said the new-look text created a five-year transition period during which distributors would enjoy exclusive distribution rights and after which consumers would be free to purchase fuel and gas directly from producers.
The industries granted exemption in the earlier version of the law would continue to be exempt during the five-year period, Aleluia said.
There was no agreement, however, one another disputed article of the bill which would oblige the Brazilian state to maintain its controlling stake in oil and gas giant Petrobras, the lawmaker said.
An amendment proposed by Aleluia would scrap that article, and leave open the possibility of Brazil privatizing Petrobras. The company is worth about $20 billion, according to market estimates.

Aleluia said the amendment would be put to a vote in the Chamber of Deputies after the vote on the bill itself. "It's a hard one to call," he said when asked which way the vote on his amendment would go.
